title.it: L'ordine delle parole: I often go

goal.sl: Držiš angleški besedni red: osebek, glagol, predmet, nato kraj in čas; čas lahko gre na začetek, glagol pa ostane za osebkom; always, often, never pred glagol (za be); pridevnik pred samostalnikom.
goal.de: Du hältst die englische Wortstellung: Subjekt, Verb, Objekt, dann Ort und Zeit; die Zeit darf nach vorn, das Verb bleibt nach dem Subjekt; always, often, never vor das Verb (nach be); das Adjektiv vor das Nomen.
goal.it: Rispetti l'ordine inglese: soggetto, verbo, oggetto, poi luogo e tempo; il tempo può andare all'inizio, il verbo resta dopo il soggetto; always, often, never prima del verbo (dopo be); l'aggettivo prima del nome.
goal.en: You can keep English word order: subject, verb, object, then place and time; a time may go first, but the verb stays after the subject; always, often, never before the verb (after be); the adjective before its noun.

say.sl: Angleški stavek ima en red, **subject – verb – object** (osebek – glagol – predmet): **Jack feeds the sheep.** (Jack hrani ovce.) Red pove, kdo kaj dela, zato predmet ne more na začetek kot v slovenščini (Ovce hrani Jack.): **Meg likes Jack.** (Meg ima rada Jacka.) in **Jack likes Meg.** (Jack ima rad Meg.) nista isto.
say.de: Ein englischer Satz hat eine feste Reihenfolge, **subject – verb – object** (Subjekt – Verb – Objekt): **Jack feeds the sheep.** (Jack füttert die Schafe.) Die Reihenfolge sagt, wer was tut, darum kann das Objekt nicht nach vorn wie im Deutschen (Die Schafe füttert Jack.): **Meg likes Jack.** (Meg mag Jack.) und **Jack likes Meg.** (Jack mag Meg.) sind nicht dasselbe.
say.it: Una frase inglese ha un ordine fisso, **subject – verb – object** (soggetto – verbo – oggetto): **Jack feeds the sheep.** (Jack dà da mangiare alle pecore.) L'ordine dice chi fa che cosa, quindi l'oggetto non può andare all'inizio come in italiano (Le pecore le nutre Jack.): **Meg likes Jack.** (A Meg piace Jack.) e **Jack likes Meg.** (A Jack piace Meg.) non sono la stessa cosa.
say.en: An English sentence keeps one order, **subject – verb – object**: **Jack feeds the sheep.** The order says who does what, so the object can't go to the front: **Meg likes Jack.** and **Jack likes Meg.** are not the same.

Il signor Dixon ferra i pony.

say.sl: Kraj in čas gresta na konec, najprej **where** (kje, kam), nato **when** (kdaj): **We go to Keswick on Saturdays.** (Ob sobotah gremo v Keswick.) **Edna listens to the radio in the kitchen every morning.** (Edna vsako jutro v kuhinji posluša radio.)
say.de: Ort und Zeit kommen ans Ende, zuerst **where** (wo, wohin), dann **when** (wann): **We go to Keswick on Saturdays.** (Samstags fahren wir nach Keswick.) **Edna listens to the radio in the kitchen every morning.** (Edna hört jeden Morgen in der Küche Radio.) Anders als im Deutschen kommt der Ort vor der Zeit.
say.it: Luogo e tempo vanno alla fine, prima **where** (dove), poi **when** (quando): **We go to Keswick on Saturdays.** (Il sabato andiamo a Keswick.) **Edna listens to the radio in the kitchen every morning.** (Ogni mattina Edna ascolta la radio in cucina.)
say.en: Place and time go at the end, first **where**, then **when**: **We go to Keswick on Saturdays.** **Edna listens to the radio in the kitchen every morning.**

say.sl: Čas lahko gre tudi na začetek, osebek in glagol pa ostaneta skupaj, v tem redu: **In the morning Jack feeds the sheep.** (Zjutraj Jack hrani ovce.) Nikoli *In the morning feeds Jack the sheep*. **On Sundays we have lunch at the inn.** (Ob nedeljah kosimo v gostilni.)
say.de: Die Zeit darf auch nach vorn, aber Subjekt und Verb bleiben zusammen, in dieser Reihenfolge: **In the morning Jack feeds the sheep.** (Am Morgen füttert Jack die Schafe.) Nie *In the morning feeds Jack the sheep*: Anders als im Deutschen rückt das Verb nicht vor. **On Sundays we have lunch at the inn.** (Sonntags essen wir im Gasthaus zu Mittag.)
say.it: Il tempo può anche andare all'inizio, ma soggetto e verbo restano insieme, in quest'ordine: **In the morning Jack feeds the sheep.** (La mattina Jack dà da mangiare alle pecore.) Mai *In the morning feeds Jack the sheep*. **On Sundays we have lunch at the inn.** (La domenica pranziamo alla locanda.)
say.en: A time can also go first, but the subject and the verb stay together, in that order: **In the morning Jack feeds the sheep.** Never *In the morning feeds Jack the sheep*. **On Sundays we have lunch at the inn.**

say.sl: **always** (vedno), **usually** (navadno), **often** (pogosto), **sometimes** (včasih) in **never** (nikoli) stojijo pred glagolom: **I often go to Keswick.** (Pogosto grem v Keswick.) **Meg never barks at night.** (Meg ponoči nikoli ne laja.) Za **am**, **is**, **are** pa za njimi: **Jack is always happy.** (Jack je vedno vesel.) **Sometimes** in **usually** lahko gresta tudi na začetek.
say.de: **always** (immer), **usually** (meistens), **often** (oft), **sometimes** (manchmal) und **never** (nie) stehen vor dem Verb: **I often go to Keswick.** (Ich fahre oft nach Keswick.) **Meg never barks at night.** (Meg bellt nachts nie.) Bei **am**, **is**, **are** stehen sie danach: **Jack is always happy.** (Jack ist immer fröhlich.) **Sometimes** und **usually** dürfen auch am Anfang stehen.
say.it: **always** (sempre), **usually** (di solito), **often** (spesso), **sometimes** (a volte) e **never** (mai) vanno prima del verbo: **I often go to Keswick.** (Vado spesso a Keswick.) **Meg never barks at night.** (Meg di notte non abbaia mai.) Con **am**, **is**, **are** vanno dopo: **Jack is always happy.** (Jack è sempre allegro.) **Sometimes** e **usually** possono anche stare all'inizio.
say.en: **always**, **usually**, **often**, **sometimes** and **never** go before the verb: **I often go to Keswick.** **Meg never barks at night.** After **am**, **is**, **are** they come after it: **Jack is always happy.** **Sometimes** and **usually** can also start the sentence.

say.sl: Pridevnik stoji pred samostalnikom in se nikoli ne spreminja: **a big dog** (velik pes), **two big dogs** (dva velika psa; nikoli *two bigs dogs*). **the old bridge** (stari most), **an old red tractor** (star rdeč traktor). Za **be** pride na konec: **The bridge is old.** (Most je star.)
say.de: Das Adjektiv steht vor dem Nomen und ändert sich nie: **a big dog** (ein großer Hund), **two big dogs** (zwei große Hunde; nie *two bigs dogs*). **the old bridge** (die alte Brücke), **an old red tractor** (ein alter roter Traktor). Nach **be** steht es am Ende: **The bridge is old.** (Die Brücke ist alt.)
say.it: L'aggettivo va prima del nome e non cambia mai: **a big dog** (un cane grande), **two big dogs** (due cani grandi; mai *two bigs dogs*). **the old bridge** (il vecchio ponte), **an old red tractor** (un vecchio trattore rosso). Dopo **be** va alla fine: **The bridge is old.** (Il ponte è vecchio.)
say.en: An adjective goes before its noun and never changes: **a big dog**, **two big dogs** (never *two bigs dogs*). **the old bridge**, **an old red tractor**. After **be** it comes at the end: **The bridge is old.**
